newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South Africa's all-share index was propped up by gains in the bank-laden financial index which soared to another record closing high as investors snapped up stock on hopes of a cut in interest rates.
Industrial shares took a breather on Thursday and ended almost square, with golds drooping after bullion failed to break through the $320 per ounce level.

"We have had a good market and it is square level on industrials. Bullion tried to break through '20 in the afternoon but failed," James Scott, equity marketing manager at Societe General Frankel Pollak told Reuters.

Interest rate talk -- views are that a one-point cut is possible by the end of the third quarter and a certainty by the end of the year -- also sent clothing shares upward. Heavyweight Edgars leapt 300 cents to a new 1997 high of 134.00 rand and Wooltru added eight cents to a fresh peak of 26.78 rand.
Dealers said that trade was active, lifting turnover to a higher-than-average 1.3 billion rand worth of shares.
Hospital firm Netcare was busy with 6.45 million shares changing hands on rumours that a merger deal between itself and Clinic Holdings would be announced soon.
The share ended up 12 cents higher at 186 cents after touching a high of 194 cents. Clinics ended steady at 475 cents.

Bookovers in Didata and Highveld also boosted volumes. Didata ended off 24 cents to 18.01 rand on shares worth 86 million rand and Highveld down five cents to 15.45 rand on shares worth 31 million rand.
The financial index surged 114.9 points to a fresh record 10,436.81 as Absa rose 115 cents to 33.15 rand heaving up the all-share index 14.3 points to another new high of 7,437.1 points.
Dealers said market sentiment was positive although a rate cut was needed to sustain the market's momentum. However, the rise in the money market shortage was of concern.
Industrial shares gained 4.8 points to a high of 8,941.2 points but gold shares fared less well slipping 5.2 points to 964.3 points.
In the broader market decliners outpaced advancers by 189 to 180 with 39 new highs and 21 new lows recorded.
Liberty Life continued to climb on good investor interest adding 400 cents to 150.00 rand and Barlows enjoying investor appetite adding 225 cents to 54.25 rand.
The market was seen rising on Friday although profit taking could be a hurdle, dealers said. Gold shares were seen slavishly tracking movements in the bullion price.

Near-dated industrial futures started firm after a stronger Wall Street overnight but came under pressure in the afternoon as some speculators were caught long and following profit-taking on the cash market.
Gold contracts were weaker in late trade on a dull bullion price.
The September all-share contract last stood at 6,740/55 from 6,750, the industrial contract at 8,563/75 from 8,644 and the gold contract at 685/94 from 697.
